Let \(R\) be the shaded region in the first quadrant enclosed by the graphs of \(y=e^{-x^{2}}, y=1-\cos x\), and the \(y\)-axis, as shown in the figure above.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the area of the region \(R\).
\item[(b)] Find the volume of the solid generated when the region \(R\) is revolved about the \(x\)-axis.
\item[(c)] The region \(R\) is the base of a solid. For this solid, each cross section perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis is a square. Find the volume of this solid.
\end{itemize}
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/bde5583e-0eb3-420d-92ec-2f7c2fc5fc59-1.jpg?height=438&width=451&top_left_y=238&top_left_x=1500)

Region \(R\)
\[
e^{-x^{2}}=1-\cos x \text { at } x=0.941944=A
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Area } & =\int_{0}^{A}\left(e^{-x^{2}}-(1-\cos x)\right) d x \\
& =0.590 \text { or } 0.591
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Volume } & =\pi \int_{0}^{A}\left(\left(e^{-x^{2}}\right)^{2}-(1-\cos x)^{2}\right) d x \\
& =0.55596 \pi=1.746 \text { or } 1.747
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Volume } & =\int_{0}^{A}\left(e^{-x^{2}}-(1-\cos x)\right)^{2} d x \\
& =0.461
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[1] : Correct limits in an integral in (a), (b), or (c).
\item[] \(2 \begin{cases}1: & \text { integrand } \\ 1: & \text { answer }\end{cases}\)
\item[] \(3\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand and constant } \\ \quad<-1>\text { each error } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ \quad<-1>\text { each error } \\ \quad \text { Note: } 0 / 2 \text { if not of the form } \\ \quad k \int_{c}^{d}(f(x)-g(x))^{2} d x\end{array}\right.\)
1 : answer
\end{itemize}
